purpose: Figure programme for the TPDS submission. Each figure has FOUR variants: 'a' is the one the paper uses; b, c, d are genuine alternatives the author will choose between. Variants must differ in EXPLANATORY STRATEGY -- what they show and how they argue it -- not merely in styling. A recolour is not an alternate.
rules: TikZ or PGFPlots only. No external image files, no matplotlib, no bitmaps.
Each variant file contains ONLY the figure body (\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture} or a pgfplots axis). No \begin{figure}, no \caption, no document wrapper -- main.tex supplies those.
Every number shown must come from data/*.tex macros, tables/*.tex, or a cited data file. Invent nothing. Prefer a macro over a literal so the figure cannot drift from the text.
Must compile standalone via figures/render_variants.sh AND inside main.tex.
IEEE single column is 3.5in wide; double (figure*) is 7.16in. State which the variant targets and stay inside it.
Greyscale-safe: distinguish series by marker and dash pattern, not colour alone.
Figures REPLACE prose. Each entry names the passage it displaces; the figure must carry that content so the text can be cut.

figures.purpose: Show that the same bytes reduced at different world sizes yield different bit patterns -- the motivating premise, measured in W1.
figures.displaces: the prose in the Problem section that asserts reshape divergence in words

variants.a: Two reduction trees side by side over the identical leaf vector, G=2 and G=4, with the differing 64-bit roots printed beneath and the first divergent bit highlighted.
variants.b: A ladder of world sizes on the x-axis against distinct-root count, making the 14/14 result immediate, with hex roots as annotations.
variants.c: A dataflow view: identical input bytes entering, the reassociation point circled, divergent outputs leaving -- argues WHERE the divergence is created rather than that it exists.
variants.d: An ulp-deviation plot across world sizes on a log axis, showing spread up to the measured maximum -- argues MAGNITUDE rather than existence.

figures.purpose: Define FBT(N): heap indexing, leaves at N-1..2N-2 ascending, operand binding at each internal node.
figures.displaces: the definitional prose of the canonical tree and leaf enumeration
figures.data: Definitions in main.tex; no measured data required

variants.a: FBT(8) drawn with heap indices on every node and the (left,right) operand pair labelled at one internal node.
variants.b: The same tree beside its array layout, showing index arithmetic 2n+1 / 2n+2 explicitly -- argues the addressing.
variants.c: A construction sequence: leaves placed, then levels folded upward, showing the order is forced.
variants.d: A counterexample pairing: canonical tree next to a legal-but-different association, with the roots differing -- argues why the choice matters.

figures.purpose: Claim 1: the same reduction DAG mapped onto different topologies yields the identical root.
figures.displaces: the prose walking through why topology does not affect the result

variants.a: One FBT drawn once, then its nodes mapped onto ring, torus and fat-tree, with routes drawn differently but the root annotated identically on all three.
variants.b: Three topology panels each with its own route colouring, converging on a single shared root box -- emphasises convergence.
variants.c: A commuting diagram: (compile, map) versus (map, compile), showing the square closes -- argues the orthogonality formally.
variants.d: A before/after contrast: an order-violating mapping producing a different root beside the compliant one -- argues by negative control.

variants.c: A pipeline timing view: GENERATE, COMPUTE, SEND across cycles, showing the GCI gap and scoreboard gating.
variants.d: A router-internal detail: crossbar, credit counters, arbiter, with the fail-stop detectors marked.

figures.purpose: Property 2: presence-gated fail-stop. A missing or misrouted operand halts rather than producing a wrong root.
figures.displaces: the prose enumerating the detectors and their gating conditions
figures.data: Property 2 in main.tex; the three detectors in rtl/

variants.b: A decision tree from packet arrival to either COMPUTE or P_ERROR.
variants.c: Two traces side by side, one healthy and one with a dropped operand, showing where the trap fires.
variants.d: A coverage matrix of fault class against detecting invariant, showing nothing reaches the root silently.

figures.purpose: Instance-suite coverage across N-bucket and topology, including its unevenness -- the honest basis for L5.
figures.displaces: part of tables/coverage.tex and the prose describing thin cells

variants.a: A heatmap of cell counts with empty cells struck through and thin cells hatched.
variants.b: A scatter of the 40 instances in (N, G) space, marker shape by topology, showing the N-G confound directly.
variants.c: A bubble grid, area proportional to instance count, making sparsity visually obvious.
variants.d: A dual panel: coverage grid beside the N-versus-G correlation that L5 reports.

figures.purpose: Distance to the composite lower bound Omega for every instance.
figures.displaces: nothing new -- replaces the existing figures/omega_by_instance.tex, which stays as one variant

variants.a: The existing per-instance plot, kept as-is for continuity.
variants.b: Sorted by ratio rather than instance, with the 1.35 minimum annotated.
variants.c: Grouped by topology, showing ring as the outlier in both directions.

figures.purpose: THE STRONGEST NEW RESULT. Held-out regret of the portfolio against k, showing the knee at k=4 and that it transfers to an unseen topology.
figures.displaces: the prose reciting the LOO and grouped-CV numbers
figures.data: experiments/w_final/W9_selection/RESULT.json and RESULT_ksweep.json. LOO k=4 = 1.0025, CI [1.0000,1.0076]; unseen-topology k=4 = 1.0391, CI [1.0025,1.0885]; best single algorithm 1.0797; k=5 identical to k=4; k=6 reaches 1.0000 LOO.

variants.a: Mean regret against k, two series (LOO and topology-held-out) with bootstrap CI bands, the single-algorithm baseline as a horizontal reference, and the k=4 knee marked.
variants.b: A dot-and-interval plot comparing estimators at k=4 -- oracle, portfolio, conditional-on-topology, best-single -- making the inversion (conditioning is WORSE) the headline.
variants.c: A per-instance regret strip at k=4 showing how many instances are exactly optimal (35 of 39 under the topology holdout).
variants.d: A cumulative distribution of regret across estimators, showing the whole distribution rather than the mean.

figures.purpose: Pinned-FBT overhead against stock NCCL by message size, including the reversal above 32 MiB that the text currently stops short of.
figures.displaces: the prose describing the cost decomposition and the chunking behaviour
figures.data: experiments/w_final/W2/v004/COST.json and data/wround_macros.tex. fp64 G=2 headline geomean 2.57x, best 1.49x, worst 3.91x; 128 MiB one-chunk 2.207x; two-chunk 1.85x at 128 MiB and much worse below 1 MiB.

variants.a: Overhead against message size on a log x-axis, one-chunk and two-chunk series, with the 1.0 line marked and the crossover annotated.
variants.b: A decomposition: the algorithmic factor-of-two floor at G=2 shown as a shaded band, with the launch-overhead excess above it -- argues WHY, not just how much.
variants.c: Absolute microseconds for stock versus pinned rather than a ratio, which makes the small-message launch cost legible.
variants.d: A paired plot of the two chunking arms showing the sign flip -- one helps at large sizes and hurts badly at small ones.

variants.a: The adder datapath with the borrow that was missing and the sticky path highlighted, plus the three repair sites marked.
variants.b: A bit-level worked example: aligned mantissas, the dropped tail, the wrong rounding decision, and the corrected one.
